ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the line $y_1=x+m$ intersects the x-axis and y-axis at points A and B, respectively, and intersects the hyperbola $y_2=\frac{k}{x}$ ($x<0$) at points C and D, where the coordinates of point C are $(-1, 2)$. Find the coordinates of point D.
ready1_open_rewrite.title: MM-Math open-ended problem
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the line $y_1=x+m$ intersects the x-axis and y-axis at points A and B, respectively, and intersects the hyperbola $y_2=\frac{k}{x}$ ($x<0$) at points C and D, where the coordinates of point C are $(-1, 2)$. Find the coordinates of point D.
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Solving the systems of equations simultaneously, we get \[ \begin{cases} y=x+3\\ y=\frac{-2}{x} \end{cases} \] which yields \[ \begin{cases} x=-1\\ y=2 \end{cases} \] or \[ \begin{cases} x=-2\\ y=1 \end{cases} \] Since the coordinates of point C are $(-1, 2)$,\\ therefore, the coordinates of point D are $\boxed{(-2, 1)}$
